NASA built this telescope to last two years.
This week, Swift finally fell out of the sky, burning up over Sumatra, in Indonesia.
For two decades, it chased the biggest explosions in the universe. One flash had travelled thirteen billion years to reach it.
So why did it fall? Blame the Sun.
About every eleven years, the Sun hits its maximum. The extra energy heats Earth's upper atmosphere, and it puffs up.
More air up there means more drag. Swift slowed, sank lower, and the drag got worse.
NASA sent a robot to push it higher. But the robot ran into trouble in space, and the rescue was called off.
So a telescope that watched stars explode ended as a shooting star of its own. Not bad for a two-year plan.
